en.title: Two DC Universe Projects Shelved by Gunn & Safran, Others Evolve
en.summary: The landscape of the DC Universe continues to shift as two ambitious projects announced in 2023 are no longer moving forward. This news arrives amidst a period of significant restructuring under DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran.
en.body:
The ambitious slate initially laid out by DC Studios heads **James Gunn** and **Peter Safran** in 2023 has seen its first major pruning. Two of the ten announced projects are reportedly no longer in active development, signaling a dynamic and perhaps challenging path forward for the burgeoning DC Universe.

The projects facing the axe are **Waller**, an HBO series focusing on **Viola Davis**'s formidable Amanda Waller, and **Paradise Lost**, a Game of Thrones-esque drama exploring the Amazons of Themyscira. The news, which broke just days before the premiere of the highly anticipated series *Lanterns*, indicates a strategic recalibration within DC Studios.

While details surrounding the cancellations remain scarce, these projects were part of a broader vision to establish a cohesive and interconnected DCU. The shelving of **Waller** is particularly notable, given **Viola Davis**'s impactful portrayal of the character in past DC films, suggesting that even established fan favorites can face development hurdles.

## A Shifting Slate

These developments leave a clear picture of the remaining eight projects from Gunn and Safran's initial announcement. Five have either reached screens or are slated to do so imminently: the animated series **Creature Commandos**, **Peacemaker** season two, the HBO series **Lanterns** (premiering August 16th), and the **Superman** and **Supergirl** films. This indicates a clear prioritization of content that aligns with the studio's current direction.

Three other projects continue to navigate the development waters. **Booster Gold** is still reportedly moving forward, despite a recent shake-up in its creative team that has sent it back to the drawing board. **Swamp Thing**, a film helmed by **James Mangold**, remains a possibility, with Gunn having previously indicated a wait for a script from the *Logan* writer. The status of **The Brave and the Bold**, intended to introduce a new Batman to the DCU, is less clear, with minimal updates provided since its initial announcement.

## What This Means for the Fandom

For dedicated fans of the DC Universe, these shifts are more than just news; they represent the evolving nature of cinematic and television storytelling. The initial excitement surrounding a grand, interconnected plan is now tempered by the reality of creative and executive decisions. While the cancellation of **Waller** and **Paradise Lost** might disappoint some, it also opens the door for new narratives and characters to take center stage. The continued progress of projects like **Superman** and **Booster Gold**, alongside the potential for **Swamp Thing** and **The Brave and the Bold**, suggests that the core vision for the DCU is still very much alive, albeit in a state of flux. This period of adjustment is crucial for building a sustainable and compelling franchise.

## What's Next

With **Lanterns** set to debut soon, fans can anticipate further updates on the remaining projects as DC Studios continues to refine its slate. The focus will likely remain on projects that directly contribute to the overarching narrative, promising a dynamic future for the DC Universe.

content_raw: News DC Universe Two More DC Projects Are No Longer in the Works They were two of the ten projects James Gunn and Peter Safran announced when they took over DC Studios in 2023 By Vanessa Armstrong | Published on August 12, 2026 Credit: Warner Bros.   Comment 0 Share New Share Credit: Warner Bros.   Just days before the premiere of the much-anticipated DC series, Lanterns , we have word that two other projects originally announced by DC Studio heads James Gunn and Peter Safran are no longer moving forward. The Ankler broke the news that Waller , an HBO show centered around Viola Davis’ Amanda Waller, who we met in Suicide Squad , was no longer in development. The website also reported that the Game of Thrones -esque show about the Amazons of Themyscira called Paradise Lost was on the back burner, though it may come back at some point in the future. These two projects were on the original list of ten that Gunn and Safran announced back in 2023 when they began leading DC Studios. Here’s where the other eight projects from that list now stand. Five of them—the animated series Creature Commandos , Peacemaker season two, the HBO series Lanterns and the Superman and Supergirl movies—have made it (or in Lanterns’ case, will make it on August 16) to a screen near you. Three other projects from the initial ten are still reportedly happening. Booster Gold is still moving forward, even though the initial creative team was recently removed and they’re back to the drawing board. A Swamp Thing movie from James Mangold is still potentially happening, though the last update we’ve gotten is from Gunn saying on a podcast in 2025 that he’s waiting on a script from the Logan writer. We’ve also not heard much about The Brave and the Bold , which is set to be the DC Universe’s Batman movie. Last we heard, the Muschiettis ( It: Welcome to Derry ) are still apparently involved though in a wait-and-see mode, and that Christina Hodson was tapped to write a script. New projects have also popped up from the studio outside of these original ten. The HBO series Penguin was met with commercial and critical acclaim, and Matt Reeves’ The Batman: Part II is also slated to come out, even though the release date keeps getting pushed out (it’s currently scheduled for October 2027). Clayface , a horror film with a script from Mike Flanagan, is also premiering October 26, 2026. And the success of Superman has also spawned a sequel, Man of Tomorrow , as well as two HBO spinoff series, with one centered on Jimmy Olson and the other on Mr. Terrific. Other reported projects include: a Wonder Woman film from Ana Nogueira; a series adaptation of Mister Miracle ; a live-action Teen Titans series also penned by Nogueria; and a Deathstroke and Bane movie that is reportedly still in development.[end-mark] The post Two More DC Projects Are No Longer in the Works appeared first on Reactor .
